clue.text: Rocket, possibly, for fellow abandoning papers on the scheme

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a scheme is a project, a planned undertaking

indicators.note: the fellow walks away from the papers, so his letter is dropped from that word

parts.note: papers kept together form a file

explanation.surface: A colleague quits the paperwork on a plan, leaving someone to talk about rockets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' strips the fellow's letter from the word for papers; 'on' places that remainder after the scheme in this across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket is one kind of missile, an object hurled or launched through the air, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Producer of magic in sungod's country

indicators.note: the magic producer sits in the sungod's name, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
a conjuror waves a wand to make magic happen

explanation.surface: Somewhere in the land of an Egyptian sun deity a magician is at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the magician's tool inside the Egyptian sun god's name; the possessive 's is not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is an African nation in the Great Lakes region.

clue.text: Artful Dodger abandoned by family? That's for the birds

indicators.note: the family deserts the Dodger, so those letters leave his name

parts.note: the Artful Dodger in Dickens's Oliver Twist is really named Jack Dawkins
kin means one's relatives

explanation.surface: A Dickens pickpocket left by his relatives is dismissed as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned by' takes KIN out of JACK DAWKINS, leaving JACKDAWS. 'That's for the birds' looks like slang for 'worthless'; only 'birds' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackdaws are small grey-naped crows, a common European bird.

clue.text: On which kings and queens may go through the motions?

definitions.text: On which kings and queens may go through the motions?

parts.words: On which kings and queens may go through the motions
parts.note: royals seem to be performing duties half-heartedly, but these are pieces making moves on a chequered playing surface

explanation.definitionFit: A board of 64 squares is where chess kings and queens are moved.

clue.text: Trendy place for a chorister to set up

parts.note: fashionable things are said to be in
choir members sit in the stalls of a church

explanation.surface: A fashionable spot for a choirboy to be established.
explanation.definitionFit: To install a device or person is to put it in place and get it going.

clue.text: The extremes of exceptional animation

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, taken here from both of the next two words

explanation.surface: Something about the far edges of outstanding cartoon work.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'exceptional' and of 'animation' give E, L, A, N; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is dash and flair, exceptional liveliness at its most vivid.

clue.text: Trick a sailor into making his Ghana trip?

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the two words fall over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fooling a seaman into thinking he's off on a voyage to West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like the voyage the sailor is tricked into, but it signals the rearrangement of HIS GHANA.
explanation.definitionFit: To shanghai someone was to drug or deceive him into serving as crew on a ship.

clue.text: Freedom of movement suitable, say, for one like Menander

parts.note: slack in a rope or joint is called play

indicators.note: say means the word for suitable is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same but is spelt differently

parts.note: suitable means right

explanation.surface: Liberty of motion is fitting, perhaps, for an ancient Greek writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Menander was a Greek comic dramatist of the fourth century BC.
explanation.definitionFit: Menander wrote stage comedies, so he was a dramatist.

clue.text: Obstruction Falstaff's prince recognised as deadly

parts.note: in tennis a let is a serve obstructed by the net; old legal phrase 'without let or hindrance'
Prince Hal, the future Henry V, is Falstaff's companion in Shakespeare's Henry IV

explanation.surface: A hindrance Shakespeare's prince saw as fatal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethal means fatal, able to kill.

clue.text: Sainted boy consuming last of the sweetbread

indicators.note: the saint eats the letter, so it ends up inside his name

parts.note: St Pancras was a boy martyred in Rome at fourteen; a London station bears his name

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word 'the' is used

explanation.surface: A saintly lad eating the end of the sweetbread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' puts E, the last letter of 'the', inside PANCRAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetbread is a culinary name for an animal's thymus or digestive gland.

clue.text: Inclination of a number to study county boundaries

parts.note: ten is a number
a den is a private study or retreat

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A measure of how many choose to study regional borders.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency is a leaning or disposition towards something.

clue.text: Sound grub, for some, on the slopes of Fujiyama

indicators.note: Sound at the start means the word for grub is said aloud, to some ears losing its R

parts.note: a grub is an insect larva

explanation.surface: Healthy food, for some people, on a Japanese mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for some' warns that only speakers who drop the R hear the two words as identical. 'Sound' poses as 'healthy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fujiyama is a volcano, so molten rock once ran down its sides.

clue.text: Bounds set for student burlesque

parts.note: L is a learner, as on a British learner driver's plate
a burlesque is a mocking imitation

explanation.surface: Limits are placed on a student's comic show.
explanation.definitionFit: A limitation is a restriction, a boundary imposed on something.

clue.text: Sheepish sort of ringleader

parts.note: not an embarrassed instigator but a leading ram in a flock, wearing something that rings

explanation.definitionFit: The bellwether is the castrated ram with a bell that leads the flock; figuratively, a trend-setter.

clue.text: Desert Head in support of American 8

indicators.note: in a down clue the support goes below what it holds up

parts.note: the answer to 8 is a dramatist; Thornton Wilder was an American one
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour names

explanation.surface: A headland propping up an American writer.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' refers to the answer of 8 down, a dramatist; Thornton Wilder wrote Our Town.
explanation.definitionFit: A wilderness is a barren, uninhabited place, like a desert.

clue.text: Military man, though not quite a general?

indicators.note: not quite means the name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: George C Marshall was a US Army general

explanation.surface: A soldier, though falling short of top rank?
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last L from MARSHALL; the surface plays on a marshal outranking a general.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshal is a high-ranking army officer.

clue.text: Little consistency associated with Ben Johnson?

definitions.meaning: thinness, as of a liquid or the air
Ben Jonson's epitaph in Westminster Abbey reads 'O rare Ben Jonson'

explanation.definitionFit: Rareness is thinness of texture, and also the quality of being uncommon, hailed in the poet's famous tombstone inscription.

clue.text: Passionate bird from Douglas, say?

indicators.note: Douglas is capital of the Isle of Man, and Manx cats famously have no tail, so a bird from there loses its last letter

parts.note: a flamingo is a pink wading bird

explanation.surface: An ardent bird hailing from a town, perhaps in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man; Manx means tailless (the Manx cat), so FLAMINGO loses its final O.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaming means burning with intense feeling, hot-tempered or ardent.

clue.text: Scholar in gaol vandalised a tree

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts

indicators.note: smashing up the jail wrecks the order of the letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An academic in prison wrecked a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vandalised' scrambles the words 'in gaol', which follow the scholar's degree; 'a' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The magnolia is a flowering tree with large showy blossoms.

clue.text: Rascal gives French department a great deal of money

parts.note: Var is a department in Provence
a mint is a huge sum

explanation.surface: A rogue hands a region of France a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Varmint is a dialect word for a troublesome person or animal.

clue.text: Worn as a beret — hard to replace

indicators.note: replacing the letters puts them back in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Shabby as an old cap, which is difficult to get another of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' rearranges A BERET HARD; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare cloth is worn thin from use, with the threads showing.

clue.text: Talent of soldier going by foot

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: The skill of an infantryman marching on.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is a natural aptitude or knack.

clue.text: Meagre imitation fur on common girl

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it
imitation fur is fake, so its letters are a false version

parts.note: gal is a colloquial word for girl

explanation.surface: A thin, cheap fake-fur coat on an ordinary girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imitation' rearranges FUR into FRU, placed above GAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Frugal means sparing or scanty, as a meagre meal.

clue.text: In France, so much crystalline powder forms a ductile metal

parts.note: tant is French for so much
alum is a crystalline compound used in dyeing and medicine

explanation.surface: Across the Channel, a heap of crystals makes a soft metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantalum is a hard bluish metallic element that can be drawn into wire.

clue.text: Some traditional or desirable entitlement of a bishop

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a customary or attractive honour for a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Bishops in the House of Lords are styled 'My Lord' as a courtesy title.

clue.text: Political theory produces surprisingly good yield — mostly

indicators.note: a surprising outcome turns the letters into something unexpected

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: mostly means the word yield loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A doctrine brings an unexpectedly healthy return, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts YIELD to YIEL; 'surprisingly' rearranges GOOD YIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideology is a system of beliefs underlying a politics.

clue.text: Source of Pistol's delight, in bed at Whitstable

definitions.meaning: Pistol in Shakespeare's Merry Wives says 'the world's mine ..., which I with sword will open'
Whitstable, a Kent coastal town, is famous for its shellfish beds

explanation.definitionFit: The bivalve is the shell Pistol vows to prise open with his sword, and the shellfish farmed in Whitstable's beds.

clue.text: Disgusting notes subject to examination

parts.note: D and E are both musical notes
something that can be tested is testable

explanation.surface: Unpleasant musical notes have to undergo scrutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Detestable means loathsome, deserving hatred.
